newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey buys first Iraqi oil exports in six years.
newsitem.headline: Turkey buys first Iraqi oil exports in six years.

text.p: Turkey's state-owned refiner Tupras said on Tuesday it had bought the first Iraqi crude on the world market for six years under the U.N. oil-for-food deal.
Tupras said in a statement it had signed an agreement with Iraqi state oil marketing organisation SOMO to take 75,000 barrels per day (bpd) effective immediately.
The deal is the equivalent to 3.6 million tonnes of oil a year, it said. The statement gave no price for the deal.

Iraqi President Saddam Hussein on Tuesday pressed the button that sent oil exports, blocked by a U.N. embargo since Iraqi's 1990 invasion of Kuwait, through a pipeline to the Turkish terminal of Ceyhan on the Mediterranean.

The United Nations gave Iraq clearance on Monday to start resuming limited oil exports worth $2 billion every six months in order to buy food, medicine and other humanitarian goods. Sanctions remain in place on Iraq.
Tupras did not give any information on the quality of the oil it would take. A Turkish vessel was en route for Ceyhan to load the oil, the statement said.
The Turkish energy ministry said it was planning to hold a ceremony on December 16 to celebrate the loading of oil tankers with Iraqi oil at Ceyhan.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said earlier that Iraq had sent two contracts to the U.N. Secretary-General that would enable Iraq to sell oil to international companies.
He said Iraq would give preference to Turkey in selling the oil and that Iraq would export a total of 650,000 barrels on Tuesday.
Tupras has an annual refining capacity of 27.6 million tonnes with refineries in the towns of Batman, Izmir, Izmit and Kirikkale.
